utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom and the annexes of this courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Pilipovic, I see a new appearance in the courtroom. Could you please introduce --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. The Defence would like to inform Your Honours that in the Defence team for General Galic this morning, we have our legal assistant present. His name is Mr. Vladimir Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Welcome, Mr. Rajic, to this courtroom. I tried yesterday to go to the pre-trial documents and was a bit surprised finally about all the confusion about Vahida Zametica, but, well, it is as it is, and let's just proceed and not lose too much time. Because I saw summaries of a statement of Vahida Zametica in the -- I saw the name in the list, the Article 65 ter list. I saw a summary of a statement. So I'm still a bit surprised, but, well, sometimes that happens. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, good morning. Thank you for giving me the floor. The Defence would need, as soon as possible, I think, only a few minutes to present the concrete and daily difficulties it is exposed to and which risk, making the defence of General Galic literally impossible. I think we need to inform the Chamber about this as soon as possible. The Defence finds that it is almost unable to accomplish its mandate in accordance with the relevant Rule with the greatest possible competence and courage. It is not possible to do that now, and we would like to present the reasons to the Court, for which we will need a few minutes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to do it right away, at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can do that at any moment which seems convenient to the Chamber, but it will take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do it right away, and I invite you, then, although I'm always very -- your language is very charming but sometimes takes a lot of charming time, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. So if you would please do it -- we know that there's charm behind your words, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The problem is the following: I'm not speaking so much on my own behalf as much as for my colleague, Ms. Pilipovic. We received, quite recently, that is, yesterday, a letter, which I think is formally from the Tribunal, signed by Mr. Christian Rohde, a Dutch legal officer, but it is in fact from the Tribunal, and this letter tells us, for instance -- and I hope I won't be trivial, but regarding the invoicing, it is not possible for the Defence, that is, Ms. Pilipovic, to charge the visits to Mr. Galic, and this letter says that meetings between Defence counsel, which are, of course, extremely important to determine matters of strategy and so on, are no longer possible because they cannot be charged. And what is more, that in spite of all the charm that the Defence is trying to use, it will not be possible for us to be as precise as we would like to because the re-reading of transcripts has been, in fact, prohibited. I'm thinking of the Registry and the fact that we need to re-read the transcripts to see what the witnesses said to see if there are minor errors or irregularities, and all this has been excluded which means, one, that the Defence cannot see General Galic; secondly, the Defence is indirectly invited no longer to re-read the transcripts; and thirdly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I have no knowledge of that letter. You're commenting on a letter which we do not know. I hardly can imagine that it says that you are not allowed to re-read the transcripts. There will be something in it similar to what was in a letter we received recently that we get no hard copies of it. But could you perhaps first tell us before commenting on it what exactly is in the letter. Because the first part I do understand, that Ms. Pilipovic will not get payment for the hours spent on visits to Mr. Galic. That's clear. And about reading the transcripts, what does it say, that you're not allowed to read them?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can quote. That was my conclusion. [In English] "The transcript is not in itself indispensable. Transcripts are a tool to support the recollection of..." et cetera. [Interpretation] Also: [In English] "...Defence team members are not in themselves billable..." et cetera. [Interpretation] And also, the preparatory discussions with our own witnesses are not authorised to the extent they are not billable. [In English] "... of witnesses seems not to be necessary." [Interpretation] And also: [In English] "... received from the Prosecution is presumed to be a task from investigators." [Interpretation] We have seen to what extent Defence questions are useful when certain Prosecution witnesses questioned by the Defence have been able to convey to the Chamber vital information such as the line of vision, things that were not established by the investigators. And the Defence will have its wings clipped, be it charming or not. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this Chamber will require the Registry to provide the Chamber with a copy of the letter that has been sent to you, and we'll pay proper attention to whatever limits there are put now on the Defence, and we'll then inform you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, two matters: The first concerns the death certificate. Before I come to that, Friday week, that is Friday, the 22nd of February, is a UN holiday respecting a day of significance to members of the Muslim faith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecution has encountered difficulties in securing the attendance of witnesses of the Muslim faith in the days leading up to Friday, the 22nd, and so that the witnesses could be ready to give evidence on Monday the 25th as well. There is a uniform response from witnesses of the Muslim faith in Sarajevo that they do not wish to be away from their families and homes between Wednesday, the 20th and Monday, the 25th of February. We are taking steps to secure the attendance of witnesses on the Wednesday, Thursday and Monday, which will require us to go beyond the proposed order of calling of evidence. In other words, if we can secure the attendance of witnesses, they are likely to be from -- witnesses who would have otherwise have been called at a later stage of the Prosecution case. I bring that to your attention at this stage mindful of the seven-day rule, and that tomorrow is the deadline for notifying the Defence and the Chamber of witnesses we would call on those days. But also mindful that it may be that we cannot attend -- we cannot secure the attendance of witnesses for part of or all of those three days. If it transpires that the problem is insurmountable, I can assure the Trial Chamber that if there is any out of court time, that we could turn that to the advantage of the Trial Chamber in terms of efficiency. But I bring that to your attention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it would be possible, if you are not sure about whether the witnesses can appear or not, perhaps you have a kind of emergency scenario available, perhaps even on other issues, but I would rather like to use the time as efficiently as possible. It's at least good that as soon as this came up - and as far as I understand, it only recently came up - you immediately informed the Trial Chamber and the Defence. So then perhaps the death certificate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I tender Prosecution Exhibit P1382. It is a poor quality copy of the death certificate with an English translation. I have multiple copies available, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Usher, could you please. Since these are poor copies, Mr. Ierace, you indicated yesterday that you had a videolink witness who would testify, and I saw that also on the list, on the source of this document. I remember that yesterday you indicated that it might not be necessary any more. But since the quality of the document, perhaps we still would be in need of some explanation of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the significance of the evidence which is anticipated from the deceased's husband essentially is to attest that she, indeed, was killed. He was not present at the scene of her death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By tendering the death certificate, I don't think that his evidence could really add anything further. I note from the English translation that the critical aspect that Your Honours were anxious to hear about appears, that is, date of death, that's item Number 3, 11 July 1993, at 1600 hours. A copy has been provided to the interpreters this morning. If Your Honours think it appropriate to ascertain the degree of legibility of that entry, it appears on the first page about five lines down. One can make out "16.00," and to the left of that, one can barely make out what appears to be "11.07." And then some other numbers, and then to the left of that, some words in Bosnian. As I indicated yesterday, the next witness will also have something to say about the time of death. She is the daughter of the deceased, and I anticipate she will say she was present shortly following the shooting, at the scene of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since I cannot read B/C/S, could perhaps the interpreters' booth inform us as to whether the original wording which precedes the numbers 16.00 are legible in such a way that they can be translated into -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. As the Defence is obliged to say that the names which we consider to be essential are absolutely illegible. The second page, for the Defence, at least, is more legible, and therefore such a document cannot be admitted, as it doesn't tell us anything. It cannot be identified. So the Defence feels that it cannot be admitted as evidence because we don't know even who it relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I wouldn't say that you can't read anything about the name. I would say that quite some letters of the name are clearly visible. But let's come down to what it's all about. Yesterday, I did understand that in the cross-examination of Mrs. Sahinovic, a lot of questions have been put to her by Ms. Pilipovic regarding the time of the incident. It has not been explained to this Court what actually was at stake at that moment. Was it the reliability of the witness? Because she said it was in the afternoon, between 2.00 and 3.00. If the numbers on this document would indicate that death was at 1600 hours, then of course the reliability question would be: Who is reliable or what is reliable? Was the witness reliable or was the document you presented to the witness reliable? But it also could be that it's the case of the Defence that death was at 1900 hours. I do not know what's the position of the Defence. I'd like to have it clarified. And then perhaps the last issue is whether -- let me first ask you what the Defence's position is. Was it that the neighbour of Mrs. Sahinovic died at a later time, or that she did not die at all, or that the witness is not reliable as far as the time of the death is concerned? What's your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for giving us the floor. The position of the Defence is as follows, simply, and it is based on a matter of principle, which is more important than the question of time: Can we accept the tendering of a document when we can't even read the name that the document allegedly refers to? This is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'm asking you not about admission into evidence, because that's what you said already, but before any tendering into evidence is there, we also have to consider the relevance of this document, and the relevance is related to what the case of the Defence is. So let's not talk at this moment about the document. I would like to know what is the position of the Defence, and I gave a few possible options before, and I'd like to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence submitted a clear document, which is a police report. That police report clearly mentions the name of the witnesses, which is legible, and a time, 1900 hours. Therefore, we believe that that time, based on an official document, is the real time. We believe it is up to the Prosecution to prove the opposite, if they wish to do so, but with a legible document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the position of the Defence is that on the basis of an official document, that the neighbour of Mrs. Sahinovic died at 1900 hours, or up to 1930 hours; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what appears to emanate from a document that we tendered, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But my question is whether the Defence -- it's the position of the Defence that that's the time of the death. I mean, I just want to know, because if you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your question, Your Honour. General Galic did not give this order, and the Defence doesn't know when this person may have died. All we know is what we know from an official document, and that is 1900 hours, as it is a police document. We were not there, General Galic was not there, and he did not give such an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we have -- we do not just have a police document; we have a witness statement and we have a police document which seems to contradict each other. My first question was whether it's part of the case of the Defence that death took place at 1900 hours. Is that the case of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in answer to that question, I must repeat that we don't know. We just assume that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is, in the case of the Defence, the relevance exactly, of the time 1500 hours, 1600 hours, 1900 hours? What's the relevance of the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say now we are going to produce shortly a certain number of documents which will show that at a certain period of the day, fierce battles took place in Sarajevo on the 6th of June, 1994, I think, if I'm not mistaken. So it is important to know exactly when this witness could have died in relation to these combats, these battles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, it was the Chamber itself which ordered the production of a death certificate. On the other hand, we have a copy in front of us which is -- well, shows some shortcomings as far as legibility is concerned. So for the time being, if there's no better copy at this moment, the Chamber will withdraw the order, which of course leaves totally open whether at a later stage this document or the original of this document could be explained by any other witness we'll see then. So I don't know whether you want us to decide upon the admissibility or that you withdraw the tendering.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll withdraw the tender, at least by seeking to tender it in the context of evidence of the deceased's husband. We can overcome the issue of whether the document relates to the deceased. Mr. President, yesterday this issue arose in the context of the Defence seeking to tender the police report. I don't know whether there's been a ruling yet on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there is not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But I don't object to the tender of the police report. I say that because the way the reading appeared in the transcript, and the way I heard it in English in my headphones, was that it referred to one round, whereas the document makes clear that there were two rounds causing death. So by tendering the document, it's clear that the official police report did not suggest there was only one round involved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. So you have withdrawn the tender of the -- of a document, which seems to be a death certificate, at least a copy of a death certificate. Then I feel that there will be no necessity to recall Mrs. Sahinovic. We'll refrain from that, then. So then the examination of Mrs. Sahinovic has been finished. Madam Registrar, there will certainly be a way of informing her that the Chamber is still as grateful as expressed yesterday for coming to The Hague, but that there are no additional questions to be put to her. Then we have to decide upon the admissibility of the documents tendered. Could you please indicate which these documents or objects are.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 360 degree Quicktime movie, P3279K; the videotape, P3280K; the enlarged photograph, P3279KK; and the police report in B/C/S, D42; the English translation, D42.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And to avoid whatever misunderstanding, the lower part of D42.1 seems to be the English translation of a medical documentation which is not part of the evidence admitted. But with this restriction, the documents are admitted. And I think it's time for the Prosecution to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I call Vahida Zametica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I say to you is translated to you in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Miss Zametica, before giving evidence, the Rules require you to make a solemn declaration. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you by the usher. I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Miss Zametica, the order in this courtroom in which you appear now is that you'll first be examined by the counsel for the Prosecution, and then once finished, you'll be examined by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any additional questions or any in between questions, the Bench also may ask you questions. So I'll first now give you, Mr. Ierace, the opportunity to examine the witness. If you do not understand anything or if something is not clear to you, just tell me, and we'll help you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Vahida Zametica?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you born on 12th of March, 1977?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which part of Sarajevo were you living in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: In early 1992, this was the airport -- settlement around the airport, and then we moved to Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when did you move to Dobrinja II?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: In May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the address that you moved to?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It was Oktobarske Revolucije Street, number 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an apartment building?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know someone by the name of Sadija Sahinovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she living in the same apartment building?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: She was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the armed conflict broke out in Sarajevo in 1992, did you continue to live at that address?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who lived in the apartment with you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: My father, my brother, and my mother, and myself, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your mother's first name?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Munira.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the conflict broke out, did you and your family experience any difficulties in obtaining water in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, was there any running water in your apartment during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No. There was no electricity and there was no water. We had nothing. So we had to go and fetch water in other parts of Dobrinja in order to get water that we could drink, in order we could use in the household.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, where did your family obtain drinking water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: For drinking, we were getting from the settlement C5 and from Dobrinja, and the household water we would fetch in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts -- withdraw that. When you say "C5," is that a part of Dobrinja or not?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is a part of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think Dobrinja is sometimes referred to in sections such as Dobrinja I, Dobrinja II and so on. In what part of Dobrinja was C5?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Dobrinja has five parts, and then two additional parts that we call C4 and C5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Dobrinja C5 was the source of the drinking water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: There was one house, and near that house, there was a pump, and that's where we went to fetch water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the street where that house was located?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. This was Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street. Sorry, this is a new name. It is Branka Bujica Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when your family obtained water from that site, did it involve any waiting in order to get access to the pump?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes we had to wait some 10 or 12 hours to have our turn to get the water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That being the case, were there other sources of water for laundry purposes?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. For washing -- water for washing, we would either collect rain water or fetch it in the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which river?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: This is the Dobrinja River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was the river from your apartment?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Some 100, 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the river from your apartment?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a particular part of the river that your family would use to collect water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. This was an area where the bridge is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the street that passes over the bridge?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No, it doesn't really have a name. It's called -- it's a bridge which connects Dobrinja II and Dobrinja III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever accompany -- withdraw that. Who within your family would usually collect the water from the river?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Usually my mother, my brother, and myself went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to collect water from the river near the bridge, did you ever experience what appeared to be shooting aimed at your area?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an occasion when your mother was indeed shot at that place?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It was 11th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which month was it?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to your birth date, you were then 16 years of age; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you first learned that your mother had been shot?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I was very near the bridge, at a construction site, with my friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that your mother was shot?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: A friend of mine was running, and she was shouting, "Vaha's mother has been wounded." And she was running from the bridge towards us, towards the building, and she was saying, "Vaha's mother has been injured."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your name is Vahida. Who did you understand to mean by Vaha?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: My brother's name is Vahid, and his nickname is Vaha, so I knew that this was about my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was that?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: About 2.00, half past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of your friend who said those words?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Aida Hodovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to her?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No. We were friends, but we never spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that she said, "Vaha's mother is wounded," did you speak to her?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No. I ran to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you arrived at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I saw my mother lying down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: She was lying on the edge of the river, in fact, in the riverbed itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she appear to be conscious or unconscious?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I thought she was conscious, and I had a feeling that she was still twitching.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about her by way of a wound or wounds?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No. I only noticed blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the blood?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The blood was coming out of her mouth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were her eyes open or closed?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that she was lying down on the edge of the river. Whereabouts was she in relation to the bridge? How far was she from the bridge, approximately?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It's just under the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any other people around at that time?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. There were other people around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts were they?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: In one protected part of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Protected from what direction?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: From the direction of the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "church," which church do you mean?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I mean the Orthodox church, which is located in Dobrinja and Catra [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Dobrinja IV, that is, Lukavica. That's the direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see or hear any signs of shooting?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, there was shooting the whole time in that area where my mother was shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you saw your mother lying beside the river, did you see or hear any signs of shooting?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, the entire time, so my mother could not be pulled to a safer area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what direction or directions could you hear the sound of shooting come from?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: From the direction of the church. There was shooting the entire time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see any signs of shooting?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. You could see the bullets falling in the water. You could hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone assist your mother?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: They tried to, but they couldn't do it, because there was continual shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I was then taken away and I did not see anything. While I was there, they were not able to take my mother out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that stage?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It was a fine day, and on that day I was in a T-shirt with short sleeves. It was a sunny day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What clothing was your mother wearing at that time?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I only remember that she was wearing a brown skirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was your mother when she died?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Forty-six, forty-seven, approximately. I never thought about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you had experienced shooting in that area previously, that is, shots being aimed at that area whilst you were there. Do you know where that shooting came from on previous occasions, shooting that was received in the area of the bridge and the river?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It was always from the direction of the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which side of the confrontation lines was the church on the day that your mother was killed?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'll rephrase it. During the conflict, there were opposing armies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there in Dobrinja, at the date of your mother's death, a confrontation line between the two armies?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live on the side of the confrontation line that was occupied by the Bosnian government army?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the other army the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which army occupied the Orthodox church on the date of your mother's death?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't believe that I heard anyone say that a church was occupied, so I cannot see that an army would occupy a church. Therefore, I object to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase the question, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which army -- on which side of the confrontation line was the orthodox church on the date that your mother was killed?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The orthodox church was under the control of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have told us earlier that there was a place in Dobrinja V where you and your family would collect drinking water. Did something happen at that place the day after your mother was killed?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It wasn't in Dobrinja V but in the C5 settlement, yes. After my mother was killed in the C5 settlement, a shell hit that settlement and many people were killed. And this is where we went most frequently to get our drinking water. Among other people, a relative was killed on that day as well as a friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that a shell hit that settlement, whereabouts in the settlement did the shell land?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It landed on the location where we went to fetch the water. This was in the vicinity of the pump.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3279KK. That's the photograph which was tendered into evidence through the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher, would you give that photograph to the witness. I assume you would like to have it on the ELMO, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please put it on the ELMO. Perhaps turn it to the witness. Turn the ELMO to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps it might be taken away again, Mr. President. I ask that it be withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please take it from the ELMO again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have an unmarked copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A fresh one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It has some fold marks on it, but I think it will do for present purposes. Perhaps that could be flattened and placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miss Zametica, do you recognise what appears in the photograph before you?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the riverbed of the Dobrinja River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned in your evidence a church. Do you see that particular church anywhere in the photograph before you?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a blue marker pen and circle the church.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the river to collect water, how did you feel in terms of your personal safety?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: During the war, whatever you did in Dobrinja, wherever you went, you knew that your life was in danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Mr. President, that concludes the examination-in-chief. The photograph that the witness has now marked I think will require a fresh exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Zametica, you will now be questioned by Ms. Pilipovic, who is Defence counsel. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Vahida, good morning. Could you tell us whether in the course of year 2000 and 2001, you spoke to the investigators of the Prosecutor's office and gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a statement last year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I will remind you, this was on the 21st of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember before that date, did you speak to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. investigators of the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you did not, do you mean that somebody else from your family gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: My father went to these interviews; I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your brother?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: My brother went to speak after me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed this statement, and you signed. And by this signature you said that this was a true statement to what you said to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you told us that from 1992, from May, you have been living in Dobrinja II?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today at the question of my learned colleague, you said that Dobrinja had five parts?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, Dobrinja has five parts as well as settlements C4 and C5.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence has the copy of the map of Sarajevo, and we have already shown to witnesses this map before, or parts of this map. So we would like to have the witness explain five parts. And if you'll allow me, I would like to show the witness the map, and perhaps the witness could show us on the map exactly Dobrinja I, II, III, IV, and V, as she sees it, so that I can ask her questions later in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it your intention to tender that map, or is it -- you use the map already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, the Defence will ask this to be admitted into evidence, but this part of the map has never been shown to the witnesses before but other parts. I've made enough copies of this part of the map, and my colleagues have this. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you collect the copies of the map, put one on the ELMO for the ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This map will be given the number D43.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in front of you, you have a part of the map of Sarajevo with -- which includes the part called Dobrinja. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- on the map with a black marker, can you indicate on the map parts of Dobrinja and the settlements C4 and C5, if you can?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I can, but the map isn't very clear to me. I can go perhaps part by part, because I need some time to get my bearings as regards the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, please tell us which street is in the part that you refer to as Dobrinja --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness was just concentrating on putting C4 and the next number on the map, and she told us that she would need some time to figure it out precisely. So if you would first let her finish what she was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I clarify what appears on the map as apparently a marker. Is that C4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see now is that the witness just has put C4 on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She marked that, and I think the question was whether she could mark C4 and C5. And I thought she was looking for where to put the C5. Just take your time, Miss Zametica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see the river on the map, which would help me orient myself. Can someone show me where the river is, so I can use it as a reference point?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a very dark line crossing Dobrinja, and at the corner, where you can see Karla Street, you can see the -- it is the corner of Lukavicka cesta, to the right. The line you see there is the river.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Lukavicka cesta is a street; it's not a river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the orientation of the witness, did I see that you have a colour copy? So please provide that to the witness. We all know that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Ms. Zametica, you'll be asked to put your markings on the copy. But just for your orientation, since on the original map there are some colours, you may be better able to orient yourself, since -- on these colours, also blue colour of a river on it, what might be of a river. But you have to mark on the other one. I'm sorry. Perhaps you may put them next to each other and look at the coloured copy and ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did see you marking "C4," "C5." Would that be Dobrinja C4 and C5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I consider them to be settlements, as being part of Dobrinja. Whenever I speak about this, I always say "Dobrinja C4" or "5."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have marked this in this particular way, can you please draw the river to make things clearer to the Chamber, and also the bridges, and if you can find your way around on the map.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The river is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you indicate the bridge connecting Dobrinja II and III?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Well, I can't really see it on the map. I would need a more detailed map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can you tell me how many bridges are there in the Dobrinja settlement over the river Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. May I get a piece of paper, please, so I can concentrate properly? Not along the entire river of Dobrinja, but only the part near Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were five bridges.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: There is also a sixth bridge that connects this settlement, Mahala, and Dobrinja V.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, looking towards the church, how many bridges are there between the church and Dobrinja II and III?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the church, in the direction of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I was never at the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your bridge, in the direction of the church, how many bridges are there?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: How many I can see?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I can see three bridges, and here where I'm standing is the fourth bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what the distance is between the fourth bridge, your fourth bridge, in the direction of the church?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: So the bridge from where I am? I don't know the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During 1993, when the tragic incident occurred when you lost your mother, you lived in Dobrinja II?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to cross the bridge to get water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For drinking water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were going for water for other purposes from the river, did you have to cross the bridge then?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, with reference to Dobrinja II, where you were living, where the hospital is located? Is it in your part of the town or is it some other part of the town?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It is immediately across from my building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the hospital of Dobrinja is located in the Dobrinja II settlement?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you have shown us on Exhibit 3279KK, you have indicated the location of the church.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would like to ask the witness a few questions with reference to the map in order to be able to identify certain objects, certain buildings or parts on the map. Can my -- if my colleagues from the Prosecution agree, we could perhaps use the other map, the one where you can see better, the one that the witness has been using.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not exactly understand what map you're referring to now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has map 3279KK, but my colleagues, for the sake of clarity, have provided a map in colour, which is on the same scale, where it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... translated as "map," but I do understand that you're talking about photos.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm speaking about photos. That may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... as far as the translation was concerned. Yes, please, then, Madam Registrar. But there can be no markings on it, as you'll understand, Ms. Pilipovic, since they have already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence will provide the map. It is the same map, 3279. So as not to mark on the same map, we would like the witness to mark the buildings by the church. I apologise again. I said "map" instead of "photograph."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then "VZ" would have to be used, because -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But -- yes. Madam Registrar, would it be confusing later on to have a "P" number for a photo that has been tendered by the Defence? VZ is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I made a mistake. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. Still markings can be made on the P3279VZ.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, with a black marker now. Would you please, Mr. Usher, take care that there's only a black marker around at this very moment. Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the photograph, you have marked the church in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us now from what position has this part of the river been taken, been shot?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Under the bridge, where my mother was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The buildings that you can see behind the bridge on this photograph, which are parallel with the church, as we can see from the photo, can you tell us what part of Dobrinja it is?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It is Dobrinja II. This part is Dobrinja II and this is Dobrinja III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You first marked the buildings that are located on the left and right bank of the river.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The left-hand side is Dobrinja III and the right-hand side is Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The buildings that you see at the very bottom of the photo near the church, viewing from the left side of the church, can you tell us what part of Dobrinja it is?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: It is Dobrinja II. The street is Avde Cuka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark the buildings with a circle, please.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that these buildings are in the Dobrinja II settlement?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict, can you tell us - and you have already marked the parts of Dobrinja - which parts of Dobrinja were under the control of the B and H army and which parts were under the control of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The Avde Cuka Street was under the control of the B and H army, and a hundred metres further was under the control of the other side, of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether these buildings that you have marked as Dobrinja II, whether those buildings were under the control of the BH army or the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I think it was the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the bridge which you used, could you see -- were you able to see the position which resembles the position that you can see from the photo?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No. It's different from when you look -- when you are on the bridge and when you're under the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the position of the buildings and the churches on this photo can be seen if you are under the bridge?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what can be seen in the direction of the church and Dobrinja II when you are on the bridge, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but I don't know how to explain it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the bridge, can you see the buildings in the same position and the church, or you can only see the buildings?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The church can -- looks directly on to the bridge when you are on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you observe the buildings from the bridge, can you see them?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the buildings, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, during the duration of the conflict and while you were living in Dobrinja in the years 1992, 1993, were there -- was there fighting going on in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: In the settlement of Dobrinja, no. I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are telling us that in Dobrinja where you were living, there was no armed clashes, there were no armed clashes and fighting, no shooting?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: There was constantly -- well, in the area where the BH army was, there was no mutual clash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have just said in the area where the BH army was. Do you know where the headquarters, the staff of the BH army was in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: The staff specifically, I can assume in the area of Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Dobrinja II where you were living?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this near your home?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Not quite near the hospital. All the buildings are very close together, so there is not a great distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day when the incident took place when your mother was killed, while you were on the bridge and when you were approaching the area where your mother was lying, amongst the people you could see around, could you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it may be a translation issue, but the question just asked includes the words "while you were on the bridge" and "when you were approaching the area."

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I couldn't have been on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't think that the witness to date has said that she was on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then rephrase the question, please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how near were you in respect of the position of your mother when you came and you saw your mother?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: About 3 metres maximum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was under the bridge?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. She was lying in this particular area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were approaching -- amongst the people that were there, you said that it was the area under the bridge. Could you see -- near the bridge or under the bridge, see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No, there were only women who had gone to fetch water, and children. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you didn't stay there, didn't stop there for long?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I don't know how long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us that when you left, your brother was still there?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: My brother was there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from your brother later on whether soldiers were located in the area where your mother was killed and when the shooting took place?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I never discussed this with my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Can you tell us how frequently you went to this area to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Almost daily, or every other day, depending on how much water we needed on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following that incident, did you go and fetch water?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. We had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- in 1993, in the month of July, can you tell us whether the bridge had been secured?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes. It had some kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain this more specifically. What sort of protection?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Well, there were bags there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who put those bags there?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During 1992, 1993, 1994, did you see soldiers in Dobrinja in those years?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the answer to the question. Would you please repeat it. The question was that, "During 1992, 1993, 1994, did you see soldiers in Dobrinja in those years?" Your answer to that question could not be understood by the interpreters. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes, I could see soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the next question you are about to answer was "Can you tell us what they were wearing?" And I think you answered already that they were wearing camouflage uniforms. Yes?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Some yes, some no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the second time, my friend has asked a question which encompasses the years 1992, 1993, 1994, first in relation to uniforms and then in relation to being armed. It's nonspecific and in its present form is not particularly probative, and may mislead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. We know that things might have changed over the years. Could you please be more precise in your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be precise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From May 1992. From the time when you came with your family to Dobrinja, from May 1992, 1993, 1994 August, did you in that period of time see soldiers in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Well, as you have been told, changes -- times were changing in 1992 and 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you perhaps be more specific and tell us what were the characteristic features of those years?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: In 1992, we were attacked, and the army had not organised in that year. Then we were able to see people wearing weapons. In 1993, we couldn't see them. And in 1994, especially not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us with reference to Dobrinja II where you used to live, how far were the front lines located in reference to where you were living? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Very close. Not very far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "very close," what does that imply? Can you --

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Well, close enough to be able to snipe at us every day and to kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, would you see armed soldiers in uniform in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether those soldiers went to the front lines?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a position to see those soldiers shooting?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion during the conflict from May 1992 through 1993 and 1994 to see soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: In 1992 when we left C4 where I lived, we were expelled by the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I don't remember. That was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to Dobrinja II to live, you came to an apartment and a building that was empty, or did you live with someone inside?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: No. We moved into an empty apartment because we had been expelled from our own house in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who lived in that apartment then?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us of what ethnic origin those people are?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President, on the basis of relevance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- of these questions which we heard yesterday of another witness. They are simply not probative of any issue before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the relevance of your questions is?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this question is relevant, in our opinion, because the Defence feels that in the cross-examination, the witness can provide information to the Defence which is relevant for the Defence of General Galic. We have just heard that the -- the witness tell us that they were expelled from a part of Dobrinja. My question was to which part of Dobrinja they went, to which apartment, and who used to live there, for us to have a grasp of the situation in 1992 in the part of the city of Sarajevo, in this case Dobrinja, because it is the submission of the Defence that the population moved from one part of the city to another, resettled, in fact. And the witness is telling us that when the armed conflict broke out, a part of the population left one part of town to a safer part of town, whereas other groups of the population -- we heard from Sadija Sahinovic that she moved into a Serb apartment, all of which shows that the population in the course of 1992 was moving from one part of the city to another. And it is our submission that through the examination of this witness, we may obtain relevant information. I just have one more question in this area, and that is whether the witness knows whose apartment they moved into. With your permission, Your Honour, that would be my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is the specific name of the owner of any relevance, or do you seek to establish that the apartment was owned by someone who was of a different ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please ask, then? I'll ask the witness. Could you tell us, when you moved into the apartment in Dobrinja II, are you aware of whether this apartment was owned by someone of Serbian origin or Croatian origin or Muslim origin?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: I believe it was someone of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answers your question, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That also concludes the cross-examination? I'm looking at the -- not only at the clock but also at my --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any need for re-examination, apart from whether we'll do it right away?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one question. I think we'll preferably then put this question, then, to the witness at this moment. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Re-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Zametica, you were asked whether in 1992, 1993, 1994, the soldiers that you saw in Dobrinja wore uniforms, and you replied that they wore camouflage uniforms. Did that apply to all of those years or some of those years or part of one year?

utterances.speaker: VAHIDA ZAMETICA
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, they didn't all have camouflage uniforms. Afterwards, they started wearing uniforms, and those camouflage uniforms in principle are all very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Zametica, the Bench has no further questions to you. You've answered all the questions put to you by Defence counsel and by the Prosecution. This Court is fully aware of how painful it must have been for you to be confronted with a lot of questions about an event in which your mother died, and we feel that it was courageous for you to come and be confronted with it, especially since the event took place when you were only 16 years old. We are fully aware of that. We are especially grateful that you came because, as you will also understand, that this Court needs to hear the answers of the witnesses that are called by the parties in order to take its decisions which this Court will have to take as good as possible. Thank you very, very much for coming, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will now adjourn. So this ends the examination. We will not see each other again. We'll have a break now. Ms. Pilipovic, you're standing, or just preparing for the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just preparing myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll do the admissions of documents, we'll do that after the break, and we'll adjourn until 5 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do apologise for starting a bit later. The reason was that I immediately paid attention to what has been raised by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I received a copy of the letter sent to Ms. Pilipovic by Christian Rohde. I do understand that there is some dispute as far as the remuneration of activities of counsel is concerned. I also read the last line of this letter: "Please do not hesitate to contact my office should you have any further questions or comments on this matter." That means that what is presented as a decision might not be the final outcome of the dispute at this moment. Therefore, I would suggest that, first of all, if what's written in the letter of Mr. Rohde is considered to be unfair, that Ms. Pilipovic explains to Mr. Rohde why it is unfair. Apart from that, there are procedures governing any dispute on invoices presented to the Registry. I think we can expect Ms. Pilipovic to use these procedures whenever necessary. On the other hand, the Chamber is aware that these kind of disputes between Defence counsel and the Registry might finally have some impact on the fairness of the trial. I'll take care that the Chamber will be informed in detail about whatever happens in these kind of disputes in order to have a good idea on where the discussion is not about efficiency any more but enters the area of the fairness of the trial. That's what I'd like to say about it at this very moment. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much for the remarks you have made, and thank you for devoting your time to this problem. As the Defence expected that you would do that, we have already contacted Mr. Fourmy to raise this issue, and it will certainly be the subject of a meeting that we will have in the course of this week. I wish to thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although, as I indicated, the first one you should address to is Mr. Rohde and the Registry but, of course, if you say, "We want to explain to Mr. Fourmy how this also affects the fairness of the trial," of course we'll have -- we'll listen to that and we'll look at this as well. But as I told you, it's not always easy to assess where efficiency of counsel activities ends and where the fairness of the trial becomes at stake. But we'll give it proper attention. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I think we have one Defence exhibit to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have -- it's good that you remind me, because we still have the photograph P3279VZ, if I'm right, Madam Registrar. Yes. Since there's no objection, it's admitted into evidence. Then I think that we are -- oh, yes. We still have the map. I had better leave it to you, Madam Registrar, because you're doing it far better than I could do it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map marked by the witness is D43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Mundis will take the next few Prosecution witnesses. With your leave, may I be excused from the Trial Chamber during those witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Mundis. Who will be the next witness you call?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness for the Prosecution is Sanija Dzevlan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Usher, would you lead the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the Defence, this witness will be testifying with respect to scheduled sniping incident number 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand, Ms. Dzevlan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. The text of this declaration is still in the hands of the usher. He'll give it to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. I'd like to welcome you in this courtroom. The order of examination is that you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, then be questioned by counsel for the Defence; and if there are any additional questions by the Bench, they will be put to you as well. So I'll first now give the opportunity to you, Mr. Mundis, to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, for the record, will you please state your full name and provide your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: My name is Sanija Dzevlan. I was born on the 27th of February, 1961.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in which city do you reside?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Since my birth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber how life in the city changed once the war started in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Well, life changed in the sense that we had no water or electricity or heating or food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the war start in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: The war started, as far as I can recollect, in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shortly after that time period, did the city become divided between two competing armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, very shortly after that. After the first barricades, the city was divided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the two competing forces that were vying for control of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: At first, we knew that we were being attacked by the army which -- the then army of Yugoslavia which attacked, and -- well, we called it the Patriotic League, which was there. I still didn't know because as far as I knew, there were fathers and brothers who were protecting their families. As far as I know -- we knew that it was the Patriotic League. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
