utterances.text: Did this group that you've described as the Patriotic League later evolve into the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the army which you've described as the then army of Yugoslavia, did that force later evolve into the army of the Bosnian Serb Republic?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber in general terms how the confrontation lines affected you with respect to your daily life in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: We were in fear, especially those of us living in Dobrinja, because we were surrounded on all sides. We couldn't move around freely. And for a long time, we were unable to contact other parts of the city because of the encirclement, and then we had to pass through barricades which were very dangerous and where there were many casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of Dobrinja did you live in?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I lived in Dobrinja IIIA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Dobrinja IIIA, I'd like to draw your attention first to 1992, was Dobrinja IIIA controlled by the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina or by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, the then army of Yugoslavia was passing through in tanks. They were passing right by our buildings. And at the very beginning of the war, a tank some 20 or 30 metres away opened fire on our building. And this went on I think until about the month of June that they passed by our buildings. After that, the Patriotic League succeeded in defending this part of the town in which we lived so that after that they didn't pass by. But the borders were very close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how close to the building you lived in were these borders as you've described them?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: You mean at the beginning of the war or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's say the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: From where I lived, the border was 500 or 600 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this also, this area where the border was, on the other side of the barrier from you, the border from you, was that controlled by the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the area where those Bosnian Serb forces were located?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: You mean which part of town where they were?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they -- let me try to rephrase the question. Were these Bosnian Serb army forces also in a part of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The separation line was Dobrinja IIIB and Dobrinja IV, which were separated by a road only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the latter half of 1992 and onwards, did you become aware of sniping incidents in the Dobrinja neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware. At first, there was shooting all over town, and when the lines were established, all of us in town were aware of the danger at certain crossroads. Especially at Dobrinja, one knew exactly where one could walk. There were some barricades put up as protection against sniper fire, so that people could normally move around from one part of Dobrinja to another, because there were certain directions along which they shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these barricades constructed of? What type of barricades were they in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Mostly there were bags filled with earth and sand, and in some places there were blankets as protection, and in other places there were containers or metal sheeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did there come a time during the conflict when you personally were the victim of a sniper?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date of this incident?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It was the 6th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: That day I had to go to Dobrinja II, because there was a hospital there. My mother was sick and I was going to fetch some medicines for her, and on the way back, I was hit by a sniper bullet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like on the day, at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It was January. It was wintertime, but there was no snow. It was cloudy, but visibility was good. It was not as foggy as it can be in Sarajevo. The visibility was relatively good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day was it that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I think it was between 3.00 and 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it still light outside at that time?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you wearing at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I was wearing brown pants and a yellow anorak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you wearing any type of clothing that could be considered a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you carrying any type of military weapon at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers or any other people wearing military uniforms in the immediate vicinity at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No. At the time I was the only passerby in the vicinity. There was no one else in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any large military equipment or large military weapons in the immediate vicinity at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've testified that you had visited your mother at the hospital and you were on your way back. I presume you were on your way back home.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were you travelling?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I was riding a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior to the time you were shot, on that day, 6 January 1994, do you recall whether you heard any other gunfire in Dobrinja that day?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No. There was no shooting. There was no fire. It was particularly calm that day. Mostly when there is shooting, we wouldn't leave our homes if we heard any firing. We had to be very careful, and we wouldn't leave our homes. But on that day it was exceptionally quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where in your body did the bullet strike you?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Through the buttocks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many bullets struck your body?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing any other gunfire immediately after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: At the moment that I was shot, I didn't even know that I was hit. I could just feel a blow. But I found out that I had been hit after I saw the bullets that were ricochetting from the concrete, and I just continued to ride my bicycle and I managed to get home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you saw bullets ricochetting from the concrete, would that have been the concrete of the street?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many bullets did you see ricochetting off the street?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I think there were about three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you noticed that you had been shot, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I managed to get home, and the people who were there, standing there, they helped me get off the bicycle and they took me to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people that helped you your neighbours? Did they live in the same building as you did?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the physicians at the hospital admit you as a patient in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you remain in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I think for about ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were discharged from the hospital, did the physicians at the hospital provide you with any kind of documents?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. I was given a discharge document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown what has been marked P3113, which for the benefit of the Registrar and the Chamber is part of the same document previously marked as P3369 by ... Mr. President, my case manager has informed me that this document may not have been in the bundle that was previously admitted, so we will go with the P3113 number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to look at the document that has been placed in front of you. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: This is a letter of discharge which I was given before I left the hospital after the treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would ask that the witness be shown the videotape which has been marked as P3280L.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the technicians could assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR: Would you please show me the location of the barricade as closely as you remember it at the time that you were shot. This is a line of yellow paint that I placed upon the pavement as a result of the answer to the same question on the 20th September, 2001. Would you please demonstrate with your hand the area which was not covered by the [Inaudible]. We will now cross the street. And if you could please show me [Inaudible] at the time you were struck by the bullet. This is a yellow X that I placed upon the pavement on the 20th of September as a result of the answer to the same question. Would you now please show me with your hand the direction in which you were travelling to the best of your recollection at the time that you were shot. Thank you. It is my understanding that at the same time that you were struck by a bullet, other bullets impacted the pavement. Would you please show me with your hand the direction from which you heard those bullets coming. Thank you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you recognise yourself in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you, in fact, meet the photographer and investigators on two separate occasions when this videotape was being made?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the first occasion when you met with the investigator, did that investigator ask you certain questions?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to my wounding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigator on the first occasion, then, make marks with yellow spray paint on the pavement?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then return to the same site a few days later and confirm that information to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you answer those questions that he put to you to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were asked to come out to this location on the second occasion, did the investigator explain to you that the reason that you had to come back was due to a technical malfunction with the equipment on the first day?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the 360 degree panorama photo which has been marked as P3279L.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your technician will assist us, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to take a look at the screen in front of you. Do you recognise what's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that photograph indicate?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: This is the main street. This is a bridge going from Dobrinja II to Dobrinja III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is this the direction that you were travelling on your bicycle at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question from the investigator with respect to where you heard the gunfire coming from, you indicated to the right as you're facing forward. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the photograph be panned to the right, please. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where the source of the gunfire was that struck you on January 6, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I presume that the fire -- the shooting could have been coming from the church that we can see in the background or from Dobrinja IV, which is buildings behind there. And those buildings were on the front lines of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the photograph be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've just mentioned a church. It's rather difficult to see in this photograph --

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- but is that church visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe in words where the church is visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: We can see the photograph between those buildings in Dobrinja II, which is behind the corner of the last building. You can see it in the background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness. In the centre of the photograph, there is what appears to be very far in the distance a mountain peak. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's Mount Trebevic up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately in front of Mount Trebevic, but much closer to the position where the photographer was standing, is a row of buildings. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that row of buildings, can you please tell us where the church is located?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: In that series of buildings on my right-hand side, on the corner, the very end of the right side, you can see the top of the church. It's a little dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the photograph be panned to the right. You can zoom out and then pan to the right, please. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, there now appears in the photograph in front of you to be the railings of a bridge. Is that the bridge you had just crossed at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what that bridge is crossing?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: The Dobrinja River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've also mentioned that there were some barricades that you had passed that were located on the bridge. Can you tell us, looking at this photograph, where those barricades were located?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Before I was wounded, the barricade was, perhaps, about one metre or half a metre off the bridge, and then along the bridge, and then the same on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the barricades extended the full length of the bridge and then approximately a metre past either end of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, approximately, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the part of street that's now visible extending into the background on the right-hand side of the photograph, is that the direction that you were coming from at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for completeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's pan the photograph back to the starting point, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, what part of the city is the church located in that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: The church is located in Dobrinja IV. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which armed force controlled the area where the church is located?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask, with the assistance of the usher, that the witness be shown the photograph which is marked P3264.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd ask you to take a look at this photograph, please. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On a previous occasion when you met with an investigator from the Tribunal, did you make some markings on this photograph with a black marker?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. I marked where the barricade was on that bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see in this photograph the church that you mentioned in the video?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the church, but I'm not sure whether I was fired at from the church or from the buildings in Dobrinja IV, which was the front line of Republika Srpska army. This was the army that was in the buildings that we can also see in the background of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd ask you to take a blue marker and please circle that part of the church which is visible in P3264.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in this photograph, are the buildings in Dobrinja IV at the front line also visible?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: You can only see one corner of them, but yes, they are visible about there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to put a square with the blue pen, mark a square on that part of Dobrinja IV which is visible on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked that location with an "X," a blue "X," on P3264. Thank you, Witness. I would ask that the usher please show the witness what has been marked as P3114.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd ask you to now take a look at this map. Did an investigator from the Tribunal provide you with a copy of this map on a previous occasion?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you at that time make some markings on this map?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please point to the location, as indicated on the map, where you were located at the time you were riding the bicycle and shot.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has pointed to a previously marked circle on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a number next to that circle, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. It has number 1. Number 1 is marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is also a circle on a building with the number 2 on it. Can you tell us what that circle represents?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It represents the building of Dobrinja IV, where I presume -- this is what I think. Whether that's -- the fire came from the building -- that building or the church, but this represents Dobrinja IV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately next to that circle with the number 2 on it, there is what appears to be a line drawn. Did you make that line? Did you draw that line?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. It is the demarcation line, confrontation line, between the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if the church that you've testified about is depicted on this map that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I presume that this is -- this black bit here, I presume that is the church. If not, then it is somewhere in this plateau, on this plateau between these buildings. Whether it's -- it could be the school, which is in Dobrinja I, but the church is located between Dobrinja IV and this school, which is in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you become aware -- during the time you were at the hospital, did you become aware of anyone else being shot at the approximate location where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. The following day, a man was brought in who was hit exactly the same spot where I was, and a bullet had gone through his heel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these sniping incidents, were any additional barricades erected at the spot where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. After that, this spot was regarded as being very dangerous, so the civilian protection was organised enough to place barricades made up of sandbags so that it would be safer to pass through that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you for giving me the floor. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, first of all, let me thank you for being here in this courtroom. Could you please tell me if the hairstyle that you have on at the moment was roughly the one that you had on the day of the incident or at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I change my hairstyle, so I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I believe that ladies can change their hairstyles quite often, but your hair, was it roughly the same length that we can see today?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No. I think it was longer. I think I wore it slightly longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Much longer?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: From this length, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Madam, you told us in your testimony - and for the transcript, page 44, line 13 - that there were barricades. Could you tell us when the first barricades were erected?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: You mean in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I think this may have been, as far as I can remember, already the end of April/beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you also told us, page 44, line 22, you told us about the establishment of a league, which was the Patriotic League, as it was translated into French. Could you tell us if this league was armed?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I did not see it at the beginning. I cannot tell you about the beginning of the war. Me personally, I did not see it. Later, yes. But I did not have the opportunity. I had a small child, and I was always at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer is valid for the beginning, but what happens later, after the beginning?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Well, there was defence that was organised so that we can protect ourselves. Everyone was protecting their own family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, can I understand that these people were defending their families without weapons?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I cannot -- I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are you telling me that you never saw -- that you've never seen a member of the Patriotic League with weapons, bearing weapons?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: At the beginning, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am just -- I asked you already about the beginning. I'm asking after the beginning. Were they armed later?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What kind of weapon did they have?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: They had rifles. They carried rifles. I don't know anything about weapons. I know there were rifles on their shoulders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the beginning, this guard, did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No, they wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. How could you tell apart these people who were not wearing uniforms who were civilians, then people who were active in the guard, since the beginning you say they carried no weapons?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know how I could tell them apart, how I could recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I suppose you can recall: Until when did the Patriotic League exist as such?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you anything about it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, you answered questions on the existence of the confrontation lines in page 45, line 23, and you said that their distance was about five to six hundred metres from where you lived. Is that right, to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your place of residence, you were then able to see the front lines?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there trenches, that is, on these front lines, either natural trenches or artificial, those that were erected by -- erected with sandbags?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask the question again. On the front lines or in the immediate vicinity, were there trenches, either there were natural trenches, that is, they were dug in the soil, or artificial ones, that means that there were some sandbags and soil -- bags filled with soil that were erected?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I did not live on the demarcation line, on the confrontation line. I did not go near it out of fear. What I know is that where we were, the civilians, there was protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, madam, what kind of means did you have?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will rephrase it. You just said that where you lived there were means of protection. Could you perhaps be more specific and tell us what type of protection you disposed of?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Well, there were barricades that were protection from sniping, and these barricades were either made of sandbags or blankets or some sheeting. Containers were used in those locations so that the civilians could walk safely between these various areas in Dobrinja since we had to go from Dobrinja II to Dobrinja III.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Could you tell us where these barricades were that you told me that were erected from sandbags?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: There were barricades between buildings on the bridges, this area that is between the buildings. For instance, you could see the -- the building that you can see where there was -- the buildings where the army Republika Srpska was located and also the area towards the bridge where you could see, also parts of the buildings as well as the church which was then in the territory of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. These areas of protection and these trenches, there were quite a few of them in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, there were many buildings. One had to go between two buildings in order to pass, and it was very dangerous. So it was -- we would have to take our life into our own hands in order to cross from one building to another. These families had to visit each other, friends, that's how we had to go from one building to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. These areas of protection or trenches, were they reserved for civilians or could also army units use them?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Everyone used them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I believe that means also army units.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know. Where I live, there's only civilians, so we did not see the military go there frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I have other questions, but we are going to have enough copies of maps made, and then I would like to ask some questions on the maps. So I'm going to go to other questions now. You told us about the territorial defences. Could you tell us about do you know who was responsible from a hierarchial point of view for the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. You told us about several areas in Dobrinja, and I remembered that there was a Dobrinja IIIA and IV. Could you tell us what the difference between Dobrinja IIIA and Dobrinja IV, just so that we can be absolutely clear about everything?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: On the road that I was going along, so going from Dobrinja II, on the left-hand side -- there is Dobrinja IIIA on the left-hand side, and on the right-hand side there is Dobrinja IIIB, and then Dobrinja IV continues. So there is a main road which divides Dobrinja IIIB and Dobrinja IV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of that main road?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the bridge that you were crossing when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I don't know such things. I'm not interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you whether the name of Emile Zola means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about it, madam?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It could be a street in Dobrinja or something. I don't know much because I don't go much in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not the bridge that you were crossing when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Possibly it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I understood was "probably." It is "probably" or "possibly"? Can we be absolutely sure about the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: What I told you is that I don't know what the bridge is called, not even today. Although I live in Dobrinja and have lived there for about 15 years, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, madam. I would like to go back to some other elements, and we will see if we can go to this famous 360-degree photograph. But I'd like to ask a question to the witness. Madam Witness, you declared, and I believe this is page 48, line 21, that "this was a very exceptionally quiet day." "It was particularly quiet day." I am quoting. What is your reference for saying this, for declaring this?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: There had been no sniping activity or shelling that day. When this was happening, we didn't go out of our homes, and that is why I went to Dobrinja II for medicaments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is the distance between the airport and the zone where you were heading for?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: You mean Dobrinja II?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that it must be Dobrinja II, yes.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't measure the distance. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I speak about several hundreds of metres, could this correspond to the reality of the situation?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: What do you mean, several hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the scale, if it was 12 metres or whether it was near Dobrinja or the zone where you stood. Since you have been living there for a number of years, I suppose you should know that.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Between Dobrinja II and the airport? Well, I don't know. If I say about up to one kilometre, by the crow's flight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. So you have been confirming what I had heard earlier, that there was no shooting, no fire, in the sense of fighting, because it was said, "No shooting, no fire." This is page 48, line 21, with reference to the day in question.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpreted] I would like to submit some documents to the witness in the English language. There is a problem. I can read it out. There will be tendered for evidence. It is the same sort of evidence which the Defence has already submitted, tendered, on other occasions, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, have you provided the interpreters with a copy of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm about to do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do it during the break, that saves time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. These are the same kind of documents as those that have already been provided on other occasions. These are summaries of military reports on Sarajevo and the corresponding sheets which correspond to the week in question, the week ending January 6, 1994. Could the usher take those documents, please, and give them to each of the parties. There is also a copy, I think ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Do you have more copies? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm afraid no. We only have one more copy. No. Mr. President, when can I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you read English? This is the first question I would like to put to you.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I would like you to be particularly attentive, because I will read you a passage that will be translated to you directly by the interpreters. I will take the text. It is a text which is presented textually and which begins by S-98 [as interpreted]. And I will start with the paragraph starting with the words "Military activity," and my questions will be asked following the interpretation. So I'm quoting 6(a): [In English] "Combat and shelling activity."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just interrupt you. What is in the lines that follow that you're quoting is Grbavica, Holiday Inn. That's the first paragraph. That's, as far as I understand now, a couple of kilometres from where the witness testified about. Would you please explain to us what's the relevance. I mean, if it's your intention to confront the witness with some contradiction -- yes, please let me first finish my question. If it's your intention to confront the witness with information which contradicts her earlier statements about the quietness of the day, then please explain to us where we could find any information about the area she lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Gladly, Mr. President. When we produced a document of this kind last time, we were blamed for not explaining it extensively. But if you read from "Targets hit," the second word of the second line mentions, very specifically, "airport." And as the witness has just said that the airport was less than a kilometre from the place she was residing, so I believe that we can ask a question, because we know that there were less than 732 shots, artillery shots, and they reached the airport, where she was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you're talking about shooting and not about shelling. But please, if you want to concentrate specifically, and with right details, on the airport, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. But one of the answers by this witness - and I think I understood it in Serbian - had to do with shelling. I heard it in Serbian. We will check the transcript. We have an assistant who will do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will re-read the text, which will be interpreted to you. I will start by "Military activity" and I will pass to chapter 2, to the second chapter, not the one immediately following, but the one after: "[In English] [Previous translation continues]... old Jewish cemetery, the Grbavica district, the airport, the Holiday Inn, and the Central Bank." [Interpretation] I will not read the rest. I don't find it to be relevant. My question is, Witness, the following: Are you absolutely sure that on that day there was no shooting, no fire, no shelling? Because we have a report that indicates the contrary, it would seem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you ask for confirmation of whether there was no shelling, I require you to find the exact source of where she said that there was no shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm asking my assistant to check up on this. He's new at this. But I thought that I had heard the answer in Serbian by the witness that on that day, that there had been no shelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me read to you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, page 48, line 21: "No, there was no shooting. There was no fire. It was particularly calm that day." It doesn't say -- then it continues: "Mostly when there is shooting, we wouldn't leave our homes if we heard any firing." That's, I would say, the first source where I heard the witness tell anything. It doesn't say anything about shelling. But if you would like to check the translation, perhaps you could concentrate on that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please -- we are looking --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is on page 64, line 20. It is expressly stated -- the term "shelling" is expressly mentioned, but I'll give you the time to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you. It's there, and I apologise. The answer was: "There had been no sniping activity or shelling that day when this was happening. We didn't go out of our homes, and that's why I went to Dobrinja II." Yes, you're perfectly right, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You're perfectly right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. I should have continued. Based on my memory, which is perhaps sometimes deficient and sometimes not very charming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will go back to your statement. You said there had been no shelling. I asked you how far was the airport. According to you, there had been no shooting, no fire opened, and no shelling in the region.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I apologise to you. I speak Bosnian and not Serbian, number one. And number two, if there had been such activity, I cannot say about the shelling of the town. We were not able to hear shelling. But if you believe that in an apartment with a small child you can hear shelling at the airport, which is a kilometre away, I think you are not right, that I could know or hear this because especially at the time we had no electricity to be able to listen to the radio and hear any warning that shelling was taking place outside elsewhere and that we couldn't move around. If I had known that there was any shelling that day in Dobrinja, I wouldn't have left my home, for my own safety and for the safety of my household.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you didn't stay in your apartment that day; you went outside, and you -- while you were outside, you didn't hear firing, explosions or shelling?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. At the time when I left, about 3.00 p.m., I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have another document which I would like to examine, 00250 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think it will take, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since I'm looking at the clock and we are about at the moment to have a break? If you say it's just one or two questions, it's fine; otherwise, I would ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have other questions, too. We have wasted some time, but I think it's the right time to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the floor, Mr. President. In order to gain time, we thought we should do the following, and I think there's no opposition from the Prosecution: The second document that was provided a moment ago is a document from UNPROFOR which summarises the wartime activities for the week ending the 6th of January. Instead of asking questions about the shelling, I suggest simply, Mr. President, that this document be tendered. If not, I would read a part and ask the witness a question, and we would certainly get the same answer. So my suggestion would be that I tender it into evidence because the same problem will arise. This is a second document testifying to the existence of shelling activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would prefer that the statement in question be put to the witness, or that part of the report be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be wise, first, to ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin to indicate exactly those portions he would like to put to the witness and then I hear from you whether you find it necessary that it really will be put to the witness. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please indicate which parts you would confront the witness with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very gladly. It is page 2, ERN 0025372, and what appears under B1, Sarajevo, (c), and we see that this refers to shelling, this time on the part of the Bosniak army, the BH army which were in the -- aimed at Lukavica barracks which is, as we know, very close to Dobrinja. I think it would be interesting to know at what distance Lukavica is, because that was the target at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague is certainly free to put that question to the witness with respect to the distance, if she knows, and we can take it from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you please do that. But you do not oppose against the relevance of this document is that -- it's found on page 2B1(c) which indicates that there was shelling mainly confined to the areas Lukavica and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the Defence is intending on confining it to Lukavica, we would ask that the question be put to the witness if she can provide some evidence as to the distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Witness, do you know where Lukavica is, a place called Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in relation to Dobrinja where is Lukavica, in relation to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Lukavica is behind Dobrinja IV. I never went there. I never needed to go there. I don't know what the distance could be from the apartment in which I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, do you have any idea of the distance, not in relation to your apartment but perhaps in relation to the bridge where your accident occurred, that is, the distance between Lukavica and this bridge, roughly?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I told you, I don't exactly know where Lukavica is. I think about three or four kilometres. That is my assumption. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, did you ever see mortars in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, madam witness, for your answer. I think a moment ago you said that water and electricity - you even mentioned food - were cut off in your apartment and building. My question is the following: Was the water cut throughout Dobrinja? Does the same apply to the electricity, to the power?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Not just in Dobrinja, but all over town, there was no water or electricity or food, and in the winter we froze. We had nothing to heat with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the following questions, I should like us to be able to have on our screen this 360-degree picture, if possible. Can I ask the technical booth to do that for us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's not the technical booth, but it's the technical assistant to the OTP who will put it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite. Thank you. I think we're ready now. We can see well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, do you now see on your screen the road which you recognised a moment ago following a question from the Prosecution? Is that that same road?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, at the far end of this picture, we see a hill. Could you tell us, please, if you know, the name of that area.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It's called Mojmilo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, as far as you know, which army at the time occupied this area of Mojmilo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know that, but this part that we see, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, you will agree with me in saying that the part at the summit was held by the government forces, that is, the Bosnian army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. What about the areas to the sides of that hill? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: The left-hand side, as I am looking now, was held by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the right-hand side was under the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please turn the picture to the right, pan the picture to the right, towards the right, please. A little more. Almost 90 degrees, please. Will you stop the picture at 3.00, please, just before 3.00. Stop there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, could you please specify very clearly what is the mountainous area that we see behind the buildings, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I think it is Trebevic, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You used an expression which was well translated into French, that is to say, that you're not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I am sure that this part here is Trebevic; and over there, this other end, continues, becomes Treskavica. Now, whether this is the summit of Treskavica, over here, where the building is, is Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the summit that you see, I think you gave us two names. In answer to a question from the Prosecution, you said it was Trebevic, and now you gave us a second name. I don't know whether it has been correctly registered on the transcript. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I'm saying that I am not sure about the background. I am very familiar with the mountains around Sarajevo. Now, whether this is a part of Trebevic, it probably is, as far as I'm able to see; and then, after that, we have the mountain of Treskavica. Now, whether this is a part of Treskavica, I cannot judge from here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Still talking about the same picture, could we zoom in, please. Thank you. A little more. And covering the buildings that we have to the right, please, buildings on the right, please, to the right, focussing on the right. A little more. Zoom in, please. A little more. Still more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, these buildings were referred to in one of the questions from the Prosecution. Do you recognise them? I'm referring to the buildings that are separated vertically by an area that is green and white.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam witness, in relation specifically to those buildings, where was the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: You mean the front lines? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many confrontations lines were there? Were there several?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. I was just asking what it is you wanted me to tell you about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me specify: In relation to this row of buildings, where was the one or several confrontation lines, if there were several?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: There. I didn't go up there ever, so I don't know exactly where they were up there. I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said behind. Is that correct, in your own language?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I'm not certain. I can't remember what it could have been in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, madam, which Dobrinja we are talking about when looking at these several buildings?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: These green and white ones?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Quite.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It is the continuation of Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "continuation of Dobrinja II," who was this area militarily controlled by?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only have a few more questions. I should like the witness to be shown a map that has been given to Madam Registrar already and on which the witness could make some indications for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether the witness already has that map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, you're being shown a more or less clean map with no markings on it. Do you recognise it as being a map with the name "Dobrinja" indicated?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, because that is what it says. But I'm not very good at reading maps. But roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try and help you. I agree with you that the river is not very prominent, cannot be seen easily. Do you see the river flowing from the theological faculty that is indicated on the map, to roughly the centre of the map? The river is line. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps we can proceed with a colour map and apply the same system that we did a moment ago to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree, but I am calling upon both parties that if colour is needed, you better prepare a colour copy. But we'll proceed now in order to assist the witness in finding her way on the map. Ms. Dzevlan, we will give you the original map which also shows some colours, which might make it more easy for you to find your way. So if you put them just next to each other on the ELMO so you can do your marking on the black and white copy, but for your orientation you have the coloured version available to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Mr. Usher, could we prepare a black marker. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Witness, are you better able to recognise the map now since you have the coloured original before you?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I would be grateful if you could first indicate, please, with a black marker that will be given to you the exact place of the accident that we are talking about today. Do that, please, on the black and white map that is to your right.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, but just a moment, please. I'm not able to find my way. It's most confusing for me because I'm unable to find the bridges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, can I help you, perhaps. If we go from the right of the map, you will see the River Dobrinja, which begins meandering slightly, and then it enters Dobrinja. And there we have the first bridge, then the second bridge, then the third, and then the fourth, and finally a fifth. Have you managed to localise them?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since you found those five bridges, and you were wounded on one of those bridges, could you please indicate for us which of those bridges? Madam, if you can't do that, just tell us that you can't and we will accept your answer.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. Madam, on the same map, could you please point to the location of the Dobrinja hospital with some precision, if you can.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't find my way among these buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We understand that it is not easy, madam. But the answer may be important. Could you please indicate for us the road in which the hospital was situated?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No. I don't know the roads in Dobrinja at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Could you indicate in whichever language you prefer, Serbian or Bosnian, the town of Dobrinja where the hospital was, the part of Dobrinja where the hospital was? As there are several Dobrinjas, I, II, III, IV, which one, could you indicate it to us, please?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: It was in Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. And this will certainly be my last question: Do you know whether at Dobrinja II there was an army corps?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: A moment ago referring to this map or an identical one that you had before you, you mentioned the existence of a school on the exit of Dobrinja. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that school is in Dobrinja I. And at the time, it was under the territory of Republika Srpska, and it is still in the territory of Republika Srpska. Or it may be Dobrinja II. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you certain, madam? This question may be of importance. If you don't know, tell us that you don't know, and we will accept that.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I know that the school at the time and now is within the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more final question: You told us that you were wounded on the buttocks?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Does the Prosecution wish to re-examine the witness, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, in response to a question by my learned colleague page 74, you were asked if you had seen mortars in Dobrinja. Do you recall if there were ever any shelling incidents in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall. There was a great deal of shelling in Dobrinja, and there were massive casualties of civilians, children, women.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the shells that landed in Dobrinja land in the area controlled by forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or in areas controlled by the Bosnian Serb army or in both -- on both sides of that confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: All I know is about the shells that fell at Dobrinja which was under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. I'm told by my assistant that one of the questions I put, on line 8, page 78 [as interpreted], was incorrectly recorded. My question was -- the page is 79, line 8. My question was whether there was something - I'm looking at the English transcript - an army corps at Dobrinja II, and not Dobrinja I, and the transcript mentions Dobrinja I. I should like to avoid any misunderstanding over this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to be logical. So you're interested to know whether there was any army corps in Dobrinja II. So just -- yes, you may --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I put the question again? Thank you very much. Further cross-examination by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam witness, I asked you a question a moment ago, and it may have been misinterpreted, as I was listening to another channel. The question is the following: Concerning Dobrinja II - and I repeat, II - are you aware of an existence of an army corps or brigade which may have had its headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that there were some on the edges. But where the civilians were, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this reply makes it necessary for me to ask another question, because it seems to me important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Madam witness, you have just told us that there were trenches, who says trenches, there were soldiers [as interpreted]. Can you tell us where the soldiers slept?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. There's no need to re-examine the witness, as far as I can see from the action of Mr. Mundis. Any questions by my colleagues? Yes. Judge El Mahdi would like to put a question to you, Mrs. Dzevlan. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me a few details that I may have not followed properly. First of all, you said that you were returning from a visit to your mother at the hospital, and I was able to understand that in reply to another question, you said that you left to look for medicines. I don't know exactly whether I understood properly or misunderstood what you said. Why did you, in fact, go out?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: My mother was sick at home. I went to the hospital to fetch medicines and to bring those medicines home to her. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. Another detail: If you can remember the photograph that was shown to you, and you drew a circle around the church; and then to the left, at the left edge of the photograph - I don't know if you remember or not - you mentioned an area, a part of Dobrinja IV. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And going back to the map, signed by you, where you marked the location where you were hit by a bullet, and you also marked, with a circle and with the number "2," what I understood to have been Dobrinja IV. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd like to see it first, of course this map can be given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please then -- we're now talking about P3114. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Yes, that's right. [Interpretation] And P3264, please. Will you follow with me on the map, please, where you put the number "1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please put the map a bit higher on the ELMO, and perhaps then the ELMO being zoomed in. Yes, still a tiny little bit higher. Higher, please. Yes, I think that's where we are. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. Number 1 is the spot where you were at the time of the incident; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And number 2 is Dobrinja IV?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So if you check on the map, you will find that the church is to the left of Dobrinja IV.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And on the photograph, the church appears to me to be to the right of Dobrinja IV. Please look at the photograph. I just want to be sure that I understand correctly. So you were aware the photograph was taking this picture; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So if you look straight ahead, you will see in front of you the church; to the left, Dobrinja IV?

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And on the map - maybe we should turn it round - there is in front of you Dobrinja IV, and more to the left is the church.

utterances.speaker: SANIJA DZEVLAN
utterances.text: JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there might have been some confusion about the maps, but I think it's no problem any more, even without your answer, that everything is clear now to the Bench. I have no further questions for you, Mrs. Dzevlan, which would mean that this is the end of your testimony. You have been answering for quite some time all the questions put to you by the Prosecution and by the Defence and also the questions put to you by the Bench. You will understand that it's of great importance for this Court that people who have been present at events we are dealing with, that they come, that they testify, and that they answer the question of all the parties and of the Bench concerning these events. Therefore, we thank you very much for having come this very long journey, and we wish you a good trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you once again. Madam Registrar, I think we could use the time to -- Yes, please, the usher will lead you out of the courtroom and we'll continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through all the documents. I think we start with the video, and then the...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video, P3280L; the 360 degree Quicktime movie, P3279L; the discharge form in B/C/S, P3113; the English translation of the discharge form, P3113.1; the photograph, P3264; the map, P3114; the UNPROFOR report, D44; the additional report, D45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I've also in front of me the last map you used and where the witness was not able to do any markings on it, which provisionally got number D46. Do you still want to tender that map into evidence or would you refrain from it, withdraw your tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, but I believe the answer is yes, because we've established that when the Defence was asking questions, the witness wasn't certain about where certain parts of town were. So I think it would be an emptiness that would be filled with meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but wouldn't that be -- we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just try to be practical. I do remember that the same map was admitted into evidence as D43. So if we would assume that it has been shown to the witness, the empty copy of map D43, would that be good enough for the transcript, or would you really like to have again the empty --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. In fact, this is a more practical solution, and we thank you for it. It would be enough to say that the witness was not able to indicate anything whatsoever on this map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So then the number D46 is not used until now. Mr. Mundis, then we are at the point where you could call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Refik Sokolar. For the benefit of the Chamber and the Defence, this witness will be testifying about scheduled sniping incident number 18 and scheduled sniping incident number 22. 25. [The witness entered court]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolar, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand from your answer that you hear me in a language you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sokolar, the Rules require everyone who testifies in this court to make a solemn declaration prior to giving his testimony. The text of this solemn declaration will now be given to you by the usher. I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sokolar. Please be seated. Mr. Sokolar, as you have been called by the Prosecution, you will be examined first by the Prosecution. Then subsequently you will be examined by the counsel for the Defence, and perhaps the Judges might have some additional questions for you as well. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, Witness, can you please provide your name and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: My name is Refik Sokolar. I was born on the 9th of December, 1953. Is it necessary to say the place of birth?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's not necessary, Mr. Sokolar. Thank you. Mr. Sokolar, are you currently retired?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, I am now retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was your occupation prior to your retirement?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: Just prior to my retirement, I was an inspector for fighting crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you have a career in the police force?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When did you first join the police force?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: I completed academy, police academy, in 1973, and ever since then I've worked for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What year did you begin your police training, and how long did that police training last at the academy?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: After I finished my primary education, which in our country is eight years long, in 1969, I joined the then school for the interior ministry in Sarajevo in the place called Vrace. And I stayed in that school until 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What were the general subject matters that you studied while at the police academy?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: In the first and second school, we had mostly general subjects, like in all secondary schools, like geography, languages, mathematics, chemistry, biology. And then in the second and third year, apart from those subjects, we also had vocational subjects, professional subjects.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was the former name given to the police at the time you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. joined the police force?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: After I completed the school, I became a policeman. This was milicija or police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At that time, were you employed by the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: It used to be called differently, not the Ministry of the Interior, but the Secretariat of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at a later date, the Secretariat of the Interior was renamed the Ministry of the Interior? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REFIK SOKOLAR
utterances.text: The entire time until 1992, it was called Secretariat of the Interior. And then in 1992 or 1993, I'm not quite sure when it changed, but it changed. It became Security Services Centre in Sarajevo. It was also with the ministry, and then during the war and after the war it is now called the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when it was called the Security Services Centre, did it go by an acronym or was it known by an acronym?
